solution_sketch: Split each term with partial fractions: 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1). The sum becomes (1 − 1/2) + (1/2 − 1/3) + … + (1/9 − 1/10); everything between the endpoints cancels, leaving 1 − 1/10 = 9/10.
difficulty_rationale: The naive route adds nine unlike fractions in the head, which will not finish in a minute let alone forty seconds. The insight is the partial-fraction split 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1); it is not a named identity but is discoverable in the moment once a solver notices that k(k+1) is a product of consecutive integers. After the insight, only two steps remain — see that all interior terms cancel, then compute 1 − 1/10. Twenty seconds is too short to spot the decomposition, verify the cancellation and read off the endpoints; forty is enough without becoming trivial.
